changes.title: feat(cli): show a rendering in the terminal as text to read, not as Markdown source
fix(pipeline): mark the step of an audience that did not render as failed, and say what became of the release notes
fix(cli): refuse a slip in --audience, refuse every argument alike, and close four small gaps in what a run says
fix(faithfulness): read a number with thousands separators as one number in the rule-based check
fix(cli): fit the line of a running step to the terminal's width, and keep the indent of doctor's details
feat(cli): put the spinner next to its label, and the header values on the column of the step labels
docs: add the changelog Chartula generated for 0.1.0-preview.4

renderings.technical:
### Added

- Render summaries in a terminal as readable text, with formatted headings, bullets, labels, links, and code. Keep Markdown output unchanged when output is redirected or `--plain` is used. ([#360](https://github.com/goldbarth/chartula/pull/360))
- Align the spinner beside its step label and pad the header values and continuation lines to a consistent column. ([#352](https://github.com/goldbarth/chartula/pull/352))

### Fixed

- Mark an audience's rendering step as failed when that audience does not render, while continuing with subsequent audiences. List release notes under `Skipped` when publishing cannot include them because the technical rendering failed or the technical audience was excluded. ([#359](https://github.com/goldbarth/chartula/pull/359))
- Reject malformed audience lists and numeric audience values, and validate `--repo` before printing a run header. Print consistent help guidance for refused arguments, identify `chartula --version` for the unknown `version` command, and clarify the output, rate-limit message, and related documentation. ([#358](https://github.com/goldbarth/chartula/pull/358))
- Read numbers with thousands separators as single values in the rule-based faithfulness check, and compare them without commas. Quote flagged numbers as written in the rendering. ([#357](https://github.com/goldbarth/chartula/pull/357))
- Fit running-step lines to the terminal width and preserve the indent when wrapping `doctor` details on a terminal. Leave plain output unwrapped. ([#356](https://github.com/goldbarth/chartula/pull/356))
renderings.customer:
### What's New

- **Terminal summaries:** Release summaries on a live terminal display headings, labels, code, and links as readable text instead of Markdown source. You can rely on the summary fitting the window without cutting long words; use `CHANGELOG.md` to copy Markdown, or use `--plain` for Markdown output.
- **Run progress layout:** While a step runs in a terminal, its spinner appears beside its label, and the header values line up in a column. You can rely on the step’s label, count, and time staying in place when it finishes.

### Bug Fixes

- **Failed audience status:** When an audience fails to render, its step is now marked as failed while later audiences can still render. You can rely on the summary to list release notes under `Skipped` when publishing is enabled and technical rendering failed or the technical audience was left out.
- **Command-line errors:** Invalid command-line arguments now show an error and a help hint before a run header is printed. You can rely on `--audience` accepting only the three audience names, and on the GitHub rate-limit message stating the request limits with and without a token.
- **Number checks:** The rule-based check no longer splits numbers such as `8,000` into separate numbers. You can rely on thousands-separated numbers being compared as a whole, while lists and version numbers keep their existing interpretation.
- **Terminal line fitting:** Running-step lines now fit within the terminal width, and long `doctor` details wrap while retaining their indent. You can rely on the line width being read again for each frame, so resizing the window changes the next frame; plain output remains unwrapped.
